geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the access-aligned lift toward the verified street edge.
Increase the public undercroft to strengthen threshold clarity.
Reduce support mass so the lifted ground condition becomes more legible.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing with one dominant bent body and a small lifted appendage, so it clears the basic form-consistency bar. The parcel response is decent but not fully compelling: the mass is contained and oriented, yet the open-space figure is weak and the road-edge response is only partially legible as a public threshold rather than a true court/entry seam. It supports neighborhood living plausibly because it is compact, low-to-mid rise, and organized around a street-facing lifted condition; however, the visible section remains somewhat generic and box-derived, so program fit is only moderate. It also resonates with the supplied references through court/void and bridge-like public-space principles, but less strongly than the better precedents.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More curvilinear and pavilion-like than the candidate; do not copy the scenic roof expression.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a carved central void and a clear bridge/threshold condition can support neighborhood-scale mixed use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: A much larger complex; the tower/podium character is not transferable here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a shared court can create hierarchy and public legibility at neighborhood scale.

warnings: The public void is underdeveloped relative to the program brief; the street-facing edge should read more clearly as active threshold.

No visible evidence of a stronger section narrative beyond the lifted ground plane.
